questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal when you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about which way you are going.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be divided ahead.

questions.question: Under good conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of choosing the right lane position?

options.text: To give yourself an escape route.
To help you receive wind blasts.
To tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: To help you receive wind blasts.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It should prevent other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a rider should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them visible.
Cover the clutch and brakes to react quickly.

questions.explanation: At an intersection, position yourself for visibility and cover your clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. Slow down at intersections. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it will take longer to stop. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic where another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Does not mean they will yield to you properly.
Guarantees they will yield to you properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles and still fail to see them.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your following distance to reduce crashes. Use other vehicles' headlights to see ahead. Be ready to change your lane position at any time.

questions.question: Shifting gears in a curve:

options.text: Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control speed.

questions.explanation: Shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can make your rear wheel skid.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Where you can see best and be seen best.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can see best and be seen best.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that lets you see and be seen best. On a left curve, ride on the right side to see oncoming traffic. On a right curve, ride left-center to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When someone passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the right part of your lane.
Stay in the center part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on your left, stay in the center of your lane. Staying on the right side can be dangerous. It may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: What does it feel like if your front tire goes flat?
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires as soon as possible.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a way to control your motorcycle in a turn?
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle in a turn, slow down before entering the turn. Look in the direction you want to go. Press the handle grip to lean the right way. Gently roll the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: What is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. A good rider changes position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How should you stop your motorcycle in a normal situation?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes at the same time. Also downshift.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph. Examples include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
The rear brake is stronger than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may give you poor grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Poor grip can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement. It can also happen on gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: When being passed, moving away from the passing vehicle in your lane:

options.text: Is a good idea because you will be farther away.
Is not a good idea because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not a good idea because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders must use proper eye protection when riding.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what must you likely do?

options.text: Leave the tire pressure as is.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to increase tire pressure by a few pounds before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist change gears before turning?

options.text: To prevent sudden power changes during the turn.
To keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent sudden power changes during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start turning. Shifting during a turn can cause sudden power to the rear wheel, which may cause a skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to reduce skidding risk.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action, then the other — brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other — brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and then proceed when safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.
